title: Publish to PyPI as squalor-slicer when a tag's CI is green
lead:
The `slicer` name on PyPI is taken (Microsoft InterpretML), so slicer publishes
under the distribution name `squalor-slicer` while the command and import package
stay `slicer`. This is the distribution half of the 1.0 release.
findings_note: PyPI name 'slicer' is taken (MS InterpretML); publish as 'squalor-slicer', command/import stay slicer; packaging verified by S58
boundary:
**Not in this slice:** the version bump to 1.0.0 and the release checklist/tag
procedure (owned by the release-checklist slice, which consumes this); cutting the
actual tag.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
A both-audience 1.0 should be installable with `pip install squalor-slicer`, not
only `git+https`. The name collision is the only thing that blocked publishing;
the plan (publish as `squalor-slicer`, keep the `slicer` command/import) resolves
it without changing how anyone uses the tool.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `pyproject.toml` — `name = "squalor-slicer"`; keep `[project.scripts] slicer`
  and the `slicer` import package; confirm metadata (description, URLs, license,
  classifiers, `requires-python`)
- `.github/workflows/` — a tag-triggered publish job
- `README.md`, `docs/getting-started.md` — switch install examples from
  `git+https://github.com/squalor-xyz/slicer` to `pip install squalor-slicer`
- reuse the existing packaging test (S58) for the build

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. The existing packaging/build test still produces a valid sdist and wheel under
   the new distribution name, exposing the `slicer` console script and the
   `slicer` import package.
2. `slicer --version` (from S76) reports the packaged version once installed.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Rename the distribution to `squalor-slicer` in `pyproject.toml`, leaving the
console script (`slicer = "slicer.cli:main"`) and the import package untouched so
`slicer …` and `import slicer` are unchanged. Build the sdist/wheel and verify
they install and run. Add a GitHub Actions job that, on a version tag, builds and
publishes to PyPI — prefer OIDC trusted publishing over a long-lived token.
Update every install example to the PyPI path, keeping a `git+https` note for the
unreleased/dev case. Register the project (or configure trusted publishing) on
PyPI before the first tag.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
`pip install squalor-slicer` in a clean environment yields a working `slicer`
command; a tag push triggers CI that builds and publishes; install docs match.
